Workplace Health And Safety: Working knowledge of the operator's HSEQ policies and how they shape day-to-day work.
Completes risk assessments and toolbox talks before work starts, and records them.
Identifies hazards in the work area and stops the job when a control is missing.
Applies permit-to-work and isolation procedures without prompting.
Reports near misses and unsafe conditions through the correct channel.
Keeps the working area, walkways and deck free of avoidable hazards.
Selects and wears the correct personal protective equipment for the task.
Understands manual handling limits and asks for assistance before exceeding them.
Emergency Response: Knows the muster arrangements and their role in each alarm condition.
Responds correctly to loss of hydraulic power during an operation.
Follows the agreed sequence for a dead-vehicle recovery.
Acts correctly on entanglement, including when to stop and call for support.
Maintains control of the vehicle when camera or sonar picture is lost.
Communicates status clearly and calmly to the bridge and the client representative.
Behavioural Factors: Hands over at shift change with enough detail for the next person to continue safely.
Asks for help before a problem becomes an incident.
Gives and receives technical feedback without defensiveness.
Keeps the client informed of progress and of realistic timescales.
Supports less experienced colleagues without taking the task from them.
Preventative Maintenance: Carries out scheduled maintenance to the interval and records it accurately.
Identifies wear and degradation before it becomes a failure.
Uses correct torque values and locking methods on critical fasteners.
Maintains hydraulic cleanliness during any intervention on the system.
Keeps spares and consumables accounted for and reorders in good time.
Test Equipment: Selects the right instrument for the measurement and knows its limits.
Verifies calibration status before relying on a reading.
Interprets insulation resistance and continuity results correctly.
Uses an oscilloscope to characterise a signal fault rather than guessing.
Records test results so another technician can reproduce them.
Fault Finding: Works from symptom to cause by elimination rather than by replacement.
Reads schematics and traces a circuit through connectors and junction boxes.
Distinguishes a fault in the vehicle from one in the umbilical or the surface equipment.
Documents the diagnosis and the fix so a repeat is recognised.
Knows when a fault exceeds shipboard repair and escalates it.
Piloting An ROV (Piloting / Technical): Maintains position and heading in current while carrying out a task.
Flies the vehicle clear of structures, umbilicals and deployed tooling.
Manages tether and clump weight to keep the working envelope available.
Operates manipulators accurately enough for hot stab and torque tool interfaces.
Monitors vehicle health during the dive and reacts to a developing fault.
Carries out GVI, CVI and DVI inspection to the required standard.
Conducts cathodic protection and field gradient measurements correctly.
Technical (Umbilical / Tether Terminatio: Terminates umbilical and tether assemblies to the specified procedure.
Prepares, tests and records optical fibre terminations.
Makes and verifies electrical penetrator connections to the required IR value.
Applies correct bend radius and strain relief at every termination.
Pressure tests a completed termination before returning it to service.
Specialist Equipment: Operates torque tools within the class and range specified for the interface.
Deploys and recovers hot stabs without damage to the receptacle.
Sets up and operates survey sensors and verifies the data is usable.
Handles cutting and dredging tooling within its operating envelope.
Configures the vehicle for the specific tooling skid in use.
Project Activities: Understands the scope of the campaign and where the current task sits in it.
Works to the procedure issued for the task and flags a deviation before acting.
Completes dive logs and task records accurately and on time.
Contributes to pre-commissioning, tie-in and IMR activities as required.
Supports trenching and flexlay operations within the agreed plan.

Running The Shift: Plans the shift against the operational programme and the weather window.
Allocates work to match experience and keeps development in mind.
Maintains the dive log and the client interface throughout the shift.
Escalates to the superintendent with a recommendation, not just a problem.
Planning And Risk: Produces a task plan that names the hazards and the controls.
Reviews procedures against the actual spread and reports gaps.
Balances schedule pressure against operational limits, and says so in writing.

Makes it easy for the team to stop the job.
